cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine prepare this week's supplier payments for HANGS Construction, checking every bill first.
First, it reads the unpaid bills and the cash. About $682,000 is available for suppliers.
It picks the bills due before the next run, and three paid early to earn a discount.
Then it looks for repeats. One bill was entered twice, and one was already paid.
One supplier's bank details changed by email, and no one called to confirm. That payment waits until someone does.
A lien waiver is a subcontractor's signed promise not to claim against the property. One is missing, so that bill waits, along with a disputed bill and one that belongs to a sister company.
Last, it writes the workpapers and an approval packet for the controller and the CFO.

All done. The proposed batch is just over $136,000: eleven bills in seven payments, leaving about $546,000 above the minimum balance. Four bills are held back and two are not paid at all, including a $14,615 bill entered twice. Nothing is paid until the controller and the CFO approve.
